title: Follow the signals
tagline: What can a sensor actually see?
description: Explore water records, satellite pixels and the colours of light.
projectQuestion: What could your sensor or satellite miss near the shore or lake bottom?
how: Real sensor mode shows separate City visits at selected shallow-water sites. Points are individual days, not a continuous recording through a day. Connecting lines guide your eye across missing time; they do not fill it.

The simulated day shows one invented order of signals: pH and dissolved oxygen respond to the light cycle before the pigment pulse. That timing is not a universal rule. RFU values depend on the instrument.

A phycocyanin probe shines light into water and measures pigment fluorescence. It is a clue about cyanobacteria, not a toxin test. Calibration, other particles and the position of a hidden mat can change what it sees. No local phycocyanin time series was verified for this app.
The pixel map uses the real lake outline in a local metre-based projection. Its grid origin is chosen for the lesson, not an actual satellite orbit. A coarse pixel can mix land and water.

The spectrum is a forward teaching model from Water Optics Lab. It adds absorption and backscattering, then calculates reflected light. Phycocyanin adds absorption near 620 nm. It does not directly model toxins.
prompt: Before you try it: what evidence would you want to collect?

challenges.title: See what is missing
challenges.goal: Switch between measured visits and the simulated day.
challenges.hint: A regular curve and scattered field visits are different evidence.

challenges.title: Which changed first?
challenges.goal: In the invented day, find which pair rises before the pigment pulse.
challenges.hint: Look at pH and dissolved oxygen, then compare the phycocyanin curve.

challenges.title: A disappearing lake
challenges.goal: Compare 10 m and 1,000 m pixels on the same outline.
challenges.hint: The pixel size changes, not the lake. Coarse cells mix surfaces.

challenges.title: Find the blue pigment clue
challenges.goal: Compare PC = 0 with PC ≥ 30 at the same chlorophyll.
challenges.hint: Look near 620 nm. Keep total chlorophyll fixed.

omissions: No live sensors, forecasts or water safety judgement. No verified local phycocyanin time series.
No actual satellite sensor response, atmospheric correction or bottom-mat optical model.
Sentinel-2 has 10 m visible bands but no narrow 620 nm band. Sentinel-3 has coarser pixels; PACE is about 1 km at nadir.
The lake is narrow. Published CyAN lake lists do not promise a usable local cyanobacteria time series.
sensorWarning: Derived from measured records. Provisional flags remain. No verified turbidity or phycocyanin channel at these selected sites.
dayWarning: Simulated day: illustrative, not field measurements. Timing and values are chosen for teaching.
gridWarning: Resolution demonstration. Real shoreline, invented grid alignment. Not a satellite toxin map.
spectrumWarning: Illustrative, not field measurements. Optical reference-table rights remain unresolved; see the precise input treatment below.
